058/**
059 * Bean context.
060 *
061 * <p>
062 * This class servers multiple purposes:
063 * <ul class='spaced-list'>
064 *    <li>
065 *       Provides the ability to wrap beans inside {@link Map} interfaces.
066 *    <li>
067 *       Serves as a repository for metadata on POJOs, such as associated {@link Bean @Marshalled} annotations,
068 *       {@link PropertyNamer PropertyNamers}, etc...  which are used to tailor how POJOs are serialized and parsed.
069 * </ul>
070 *
071 * <p>
072 * All serializers and parsers use this context so that they can handle POJOs using a common framework.
073 *
074 * <h5 class='topic'>Bean Contexts</h5>
075 *
076 * <p>
077 * Bean contexts are created through the {@link MarshallingContext#create() MarshallingContext.create()} and {@link Builder#build()} methods.
078 * <br>These context objects are read-only, reusable, and thread-safe.
079 *
080 * <p>
081 * Each bean context maintains a cache of {@link ClassMeta} objects that describe information about classes encountered.
082 * These <c>ClassMeta</c> objects are time-consuming to construct.
083 * Therefore, instances of {@link MarshallingContext} that share the same <js>"MarshallingContext.*"</js> property values share
084 * the same cache.  This allows for efficient reuse of <c>ClassMeta</c> objects so that the information about
085 * classes only needs to be calculated once.
086 * Because of this, many of the properties defined on the {@link MarshallingContext} class cannot be overridden on the session.
087 *
088 * <h5 class='topic'>Bean Sessions</h5>
089 *
090 * <p>
091 * Whereas <c>MarshallingContext</c> objects are permanent, unchangeable, cached, and thread-safe,
092 * {@link MarshallingSession} objects are ephemeral and not thread-safe.
093 * They are meant to be used as quickly-constructed scratchpads for creating bean maps.
094 * {@link BeanMap} objects can only be created through the session.
095 *
096 * <h5 class='topic'>MarshallingContext configuration properties</h5>
097 *
098 * <p>
099 * <c>BeanContexts</c> have several configuration properties that can be used to tweak behavior on how beans are
100 * handled.  These are denoted as the static <jsf>BEAN_*</jsf> fields on this class.
101 *
102 * <p>
103 * Some settings (e.g. {@link Builder#beansRequireDefaultConstructor()}) are used to differentiate between bean
104 * and non-bean classes.
105 * Attempting to create a bean map around one of these objects will throw a {@link BeanRuntimeException}.
106 * The purpose for this behavior is so that the serializers can identify these non-bean classes and convert them to
107 * plain strings using the {@link Object#toString()} method.
108 *
109 * <p>
110 * Some settings (e.g. {@link Builder#beanFieldVisibility(Visibility)}) are used to determine what kinds of properties are
111 * detected on beans.
112 *
113 * <p>
114 * Some settings (e.g. {@link Builder#beanMapPutReturnsOldValue()}) change the runtime behavior of bean maps.
115 *
116 * <h5 class='section'>Example:</h5>
117 *
118 * <p class='bjava'>
119 *    <jc>// Construct a context from scratch.</jc>
120 *    MarshallingContext <jv>marshallingContext</jv> = MarshallingContext
121 *       .<jsm>create</jsm>()
122 *       .beansRequireDefaultConstructor()
123 *       .notBeanClasses(Foo.<jk>class</jk>)
124 *       .build();
125 * </p>
126 *
127 * <h5 class='topic'>Bean Maps</h5>
128 *
129 * <p>
130 * {@link BeanMap BeanMaps} are wrappers around Java beans that allow properties to be retrieved and
131 * set using the common {@link Map#put(Object,Object)} and {@link Map#get(Object)} methods.
132 *
133 * <p>
134 * Bean maps are created in two ways...
135 * <ol>
136 *    <li>{@link MarshallingSession#toBeanMap(Object) MarshallingSession.toBeanMap()} - Wraps an existing bean inside a {@code Map}
137 *       wrapper.
138 *    <li>{@link MarshallingSession#newBeanMap(Class) MarshallingSession.newBeanMap()} - Create a new bean instance wrapped in a
139 *       {@code Map} wrapper.
140 * </ol>
141 *
142 * <h5 class='section'>Example:</h5>
143 *
144 * <p class='bjava'>
145 *    <jc>// A sample bean class</jc>
146 *    <jk>public class</jk> Person {
147 *       <jk>public</jk> String getName();
148 *       <jk>public void</jk> setName(String <jv>name</jv>);
149 *       <jk>public int</jk> getAge();
150 *       <jk>public void</jk> setAge(<jk>int</jk> <jv>age</jv>);
151 *    }
152 *
153 *    <jc>// Create a new bean session</jc>
154 *    MarshallingSession <jv>session</jv> = MarshallingContext.<jsf>DEFAULT</jsf>.createSession();
155 *
156 *    <jc>// Wrap an existing bean in a new bean map</jc>
157 *    BeanMap&lt;Person&gt; <jv>map1</jv> = <jv>session</jv>.toBeanMap(<jk>new</jk> Person());
158 *    <jv>map1</jv>.put(<js>"name"</js>, <js>"John Smith"</js>);
159 *    <jv>map1</jv>.put(<js>"age"</js>, 45);
160 *
161 *    <jc>// Create a new bean instance wrapped in a new bean map</jc>
162 *    BeanMap&lt;Person&gt; <jv>map2</jv> = <jv>session</jv>.newBeanMap(Person.<jk>class</jk>);
163 *    <jv>map2</jv>.put(<js>"name"</js>, <js>"John Smith"</js>);
164 *    <jv>map2</jv>.put(<js>"age"</js>, 45);
165 *    Person <jv>person</jv> = <jv>map2</jv>.getBean();  <jc>// Get the bean instance that was created.</jc>
166 * </p>
167 *
168 * <h5 class='section'>Notes:</h5><ul>
169 *    <li class='note'>This class is thread safe and reusable.
170 * </ul>
171 *
172 * <h5 class='section'>See Also:</h5><ul>
173 *    <li class='link'><a class="doclink" href="https://juneau.apache.org/docs/topics/BeanContexts">Bean Contexts</a>
174 * </ul>
175 */
176@SuppressWarnings({
177   "java:S1192", // Duplicated literals (argument/property names) read more clearly inline than as constants
178   "java:S1452", // Wildcard required - ClassMeta<?> for parameter resolution and type variables
179   "java:S1612", // Lambdas used instead of method references for readability in complex chained expressions
180   "java:S3776", // findConversion() registers the whole conversion matrix in one method, and resolveClassMeta(Type, ...) dispatches over every Type shape
181   "java:S6539", // Monster class; MarshallingContext is intentionally the central bean-context configuration hub (also covers Collection.toArray() usage)
182   "rawtypes", // Raw types necessary for generic type handling
183   "unchecked" // Type erasure requires unchecked casts
184})
185public class MarshallingContext extends Context implements ConversionFinder, BeanTypeResolver {

194      private static int integer(boolean...values) {
195         var n = 0;
196         for (var b : values)
197            n = (n << 1) | (b ? 1 : 0);
198         return n;
199      }

428      /**
429       * Minimum bean class visibility.
430       *
431       * <p>
432       * Classes are not considered beans unless they meet the minimum visibility requirements.
433       * For example, if the visibility is <jsf>PUBLIC</jsf> and the bean class is <jk>protected</jk>, then the class
434       * will not be interpreted as a bean class and be serialized as a string.
435       * Use this setting to reduce the visibility requirement.
436       *
437       * <h5 class='section'>Example:</h5>
438       * <p class='bjava'>
439       *    <jc>// A bean with a protected class and one field.</jc>
440       *    <jk>protected class</jk> MyBean {
441       *       <jk>public</jk> String <jf>foo</jf> = <js>"bar"</js>;
442       *    }
443       *
444       *    <jc>// Create a serializer that's capable of serializing the class.</jc>
445       *    WriterSerializer <jv>serializer</jv> = JsonSerializer
446       *       .<jsm>create</jsm>()
447       *       .beanClassVisibility(<jsf>PROTECTED</jsf>)
448       *       .build();
449       *
450       *    <jc>// Produces:  {"foo","bar"}</jc>
451       *    String <jv>json</jv> = <jv>serializer</jv>.write(<jk>new</jk> MyBean());
452       * </p>
453       *
454       * <h5 class='section'>Notes:</h5><ul>
455       *    <li class='note'>The {@link Bean @Marshalled} annotation can be used on a non-public bean class to override this setting.
456       *    <li class='note'>The {@link BeanIgnore @BeanIgnore} annotation can also be used on a public bean class to ignore it as a bean.
457       * </ul>
458       *
459       * <h5 class='section'>See Also:</h5><ul>
460       *    <li class='ja'>{@link BeanConfig#beanClassVisibility()}
461       * </ul>
462       *
463       * @param value
464       *    The new value for this setting.
465       *    <br>The default is {@link Visibility#PUBLIC}.
466       *    <br>Cannot be <jk>null</jk>.
467       * @return This object.
468       */
469      public Builder beanClassVisibility(Visibility value) {
470         beanClassVisibility = reqnn("value", value);
471         return this;
472      }
473
474      /**
475       * Minimum bean constructor visibility.
476       *
477       * <p>
478       * Only look for constructors with the specified minimum visibility.
479       *
480       * <p>
481       * This setting affects the logic for finding no-arg constructors for bean.  Normally, only <jk>public</jk> no-arg
482       * constructors are used.  Use this setting if you want to reduce the visibility requirement.
483       *
484       * <h5 class='section'>Example:</h5>
485       * <p class='bjava'>
486       *    <jc>// A bean with a protected constructor and one field.</jc>
487       *    <jk>public class</jk> MyBean {
488       *       <jk>public</jk> String <jf>foo</jf>;
489       *
490       *       <jk>protected</jk> MyBean() {}
491       *    }
492       *
493       *    <jc>// Create a parser capable of calling the protected constructor.</jc>
494       *    ReaderParser <jv>parser</jv> = ReaderParser
495       *       .<jsm>create</jsm>()
496       *       .beanConstructorVisibility(<jsf>PROTECTED</jsf>)
497       *       .build();
498       *
499       *    <jc>// Use it.</jc>
500       *    MyBean <jv>myBean</jv> = <jv>parser</jv>.read(<js>"{foo:'bar'}"</js>, MyBean.<jk>class</jk>);
501       * </p>
502       *
503       * <h5 class='section'>Notes:</h5><ul>
504       *    <li class='note'>The {@link BeanCtor @BeanCtor} annotation can also be used to expose a non-public constructor.
505       *    <li class='note'>The {@link BeanIgnore @BeanIgnore} annotation can also be used on a public bean constructor to ignore it.
506       * </ul>
507       *
508       * <h5 class='section'>See Also:</h5><ul>
509       *    <li class='ja'>{@link BeanConfig#beanConstructorVisibility()}
510       * </ul>
511       *
512       * @param value
513       *    The new value for this setting.
514       *    <br>The default is {@link Visibility#PUBLIC}.
515       *    <br>Cannot be <jk>null</jk>.
516       * @return This object.
517       */
518      public Builder beanConstructorVisibility(Visibility value) {
519         beanConstructorVisibility = reqnn("value", value);
520         return this;
521      }

540       *    The values to add to this setting.

543       * @see #beanDictionary(ClassInfo...)
544       */
545      public Builder beanDictionary(Class<?>...values) {
546         reqnns("values", values);
547         return beanDictionary(Stream.of(values).map(x -> info(x)).toArray(ClassInfo[]::new));
548      }

550      /**
551       * Bean dictionary.
552       *
553       * <p>
554       * The list of classes that make up the bean dictionary in this bean context.
555       *
556       * <p>
557       * Values are prepended to the list so that later calls can override classes of earlier calls.
558       *
559       * <p>
560       * A dictionary is a name/class mapping used to find class types during parsing when they cannot be inferred
561       * through reflection.  The names are defined through the {@link Marshalled#typeName() @Marshalled(typeName)} annotation defined
562       * on the bean class.  For example, if a class <c>Foo</c> has a type-name of <js>"myfoo"</js>, then it would end up
563       * serialized as <js>"{_type:'myfoo',...}"</js> in JSON
564       * or <js>"&lt;myfoo&gt;...&lt;/myfoo&gt;"</js> in XML.
565       *
566       * <p>
567       * This setting tells the parsers which classes to look for when resolving <js>"_type"</js> attributes.
568       *
569       * <p>
570       * Values can consist of any of the following types:
571       * <ul>
572       *    <li>Any bean class that specifies a value for {@link Marshalled#typeName() @Marshalled(typeName)}.
573       *    <li>Any subclass of {@link BeanDictionaryList} containing a collection of bean classes with type name annotations.
574       *    <li>Any subclass of {@link BeanDictionaryMap} containing a mapping of type names to classes without type name annotations.
575       *    <li>Any array or collection of the objects above.
576       * </ul>
577       *
578       * <h5 class='section'>Example:</h5>
579       * <p class='bjava'>
580       *    <jc>// POJOs with @Marshalled(name) annotations.</jc>
581       *    <ja>@Marshalled</ja>(typeName=<js>"foo"</js>)
582       *    <jk>public class</jk> Foo {...}
583       *    <ja>@Marshalled</ja>(typeName=<js>"bar"</js>)
584       *    <jk>public class</jk> Bar {...}
585       *
586       *    <jc>// Create a parser and tell it which classes to try to resolve.</jc>
587       *    ReaderParser <jv>parser</jv> = JsonParser
588       *       .<jsm>create</jsm>()
589       *       .dictionary(Foo.<jk>class</jk>, Bar.<jk>class</jk>)
590       *       .addBeanTypes()
591       *       .build();
592       *
593       *    <jc>// A bean with a field with an indeterminate type.</jc>
594       *    <jk>public class</jk> MyBean {
595       *       <jk>public</jk> Object <jf>mySimpleField</jf>;
596       *    }
597       *
598       *    <jc>// Parse bean.</jc>
599       *    MyBean <jv>myBean</jv> = <jv>parser</jv>.read(<js>"{mySimpleField:{_type:'foo',...}}"</js>, MyBean.<jk>class</jk>);
600       * </p>
601       *
602       * <p>
603       * Another option is to use the {@link Marshalled#dictionary()} annotation on the POJO class itself:
604       *
605       * <p class='bjava'>
606       *    <jc>// Instead of by parser, define a bean dictionary on a class through an annotation.</jc>
607       *    <jc>// This applies to all properties on this class and all subclasses.</jc>
608       *    <ja>@Marshalled</ja>(dictionary={Foo.<jk>class</jk>,Bar.<jk>class</jk>})
609       *    <jk>public class</jk> MyBean {
610       *       <jk>public</jk> Object <jf>mySimpleField</jf>;  <jc>// May contain Foo or Bar object.</jc>
611       *       <jk>public</jk> Map&lt;String,Object&gt; <jf>myMapField</jf>;  <jc>// May contain Foo or Bar objects.</jc>
612       *    }
613       * </p>
614       *
615       * <p>
616       *    A typical usage is to allow for HTML documents to be parsed back into HTML beans:
617       * <p class='bjava'>
618       *    <jc>// Use the predefined HTML5 bean dictionary which is a BeanDictionaryList.</jc>
619       *    ReaderParser <jv>parser</jv> = HtmlParser
620       *       .<jsm>create</jsm>()
621       *       .dictionary(HtmlBeanDictionary.<jk>class</jk>)
622       *       .build();
623       *
624       *    <jc>// Parse an HTML body into HTML beans.</jc>
625       *    Body <jv>body</jv> = <jv>parser</jv>.read(<js>"&lt;body&gt;&lt;ul&gt;&lt;li&gt;foo&lt;/li&gt;&lt;li&gt;bar&lt;/li&gt;&lt;/ul&gt;"</js>, Body.<jk>class</jk>);
626       * </p>
627       *
628       * <h5 class='section'>See Also:</h5><ul>
629       *    <li class='ja'>{@link Marshalled#dictionary()}
630       *    <li class='ja'>{@link MarshalledProp#dictionary()}
631       *    <li class='ja'>{@link MarshalledConfig#dictionary()}
632       *    <li class='ja'>{@link MarshalledConfig#dictionary_replace()}
633       *    <li class='jm'>{@link MarshallingContext.Builder#beanDictionary(ClassInfo...)}
634       * </ul>
635       *
636       * @param values
637       *    The values to add to this setting.
638       *    <br>Cannot contain <jk>null</jk> values.
639       * @return This object.
640       */
641      public Builder beanDictionary(ClassInfo...values) {
642         reqnns("values", values);
643         return beanDictionary(l(values));
644      }
645
646      /**
647       * Same as {@link #beanDictionary(ClassInfo...)} but allows you to pass in a collection of class info objects.
648       *
649       * @param values
650       *    The values to add to this setting.
651       *    <br>Cannot be <jk>null</jk> or contain <jk>null</jk> values.
652       * @return This object.
653       * @see #beanDictionary(ClassInfo...)
654       */
655      public Builder beanDictionary(Collection<ClassInfo> values) {
656         reqnns("values", values);
657         beanDictionary().addAll(0, values);
658         return this;
659      }

661      /**
662       * Minimum bean field visibility.
663       *
664       * <p>
665       * Only look for bean fields with the specified minimum visibility.
666       *
667       * <p>
668       * This affects which fields on a bean class are considered bean properties.  Normally only <jk>public</jk> fields are considered.
669       * Use this setting if you want to reduce the visibility requirement.
670       *
671       * <h5 class='section'>Example:</h5>
672       * <p class='bjava'>
673       *    <jc>// A bean with a protected field.</jc>
674       *    <jk>public class</jk> MyBean {
675       *       <jk>protected</jk> String <jf>foo</jf> = <js>"bar"</js>;
676       *    }
677       *
678       *    <jc>// Create a serializer that recognizes the protected field.</jc>
679       *    WriterSerializer <jv>serializer</jv> = JsonSerializer
680       *       .<jsm>create</jsm>()
681       *       .beanFieldVisibility(<jsf>PROTECTED</jsf>)
682       *       .build();
683       *
684       *    <jc>// Produces:  {"foo":"bar"}</jc>
685       *    String <jv>json</jv> = <jv>serializer</jv>.write(<jk>new</jk> MyBean());
686       * </p>
687       *
688       * <p>
689       * Bean fields can be ignored as properties entirely by setting the value to {@link Visibility#NONE}
690       *
691       * <p class='bjava'>
692       *    <jc>// Disable using fields as properties entirely.</jc>
693       *    WriterSerializer <jv>serializer</jv> = JsonSerializer
694       *       .<jsm>create</jsm>()
695       *       .beanFieldVisibility(<jsf>NONE</jsf>)
696       *       .build();
697       * </p>
698       *
699       * <h5 class='section'>Notes:</h5><ul>
700       *    <li class='note'>The {@link BeanProp @BeanProp} annotation can also be used to expose a non-public field.
701       *    <li class='note'>The {@link BeanIgnore @BeanIgnore} annotation can also be used on a public bean field to ignore it as a bean property.
702       * </ul>
703       *
704       * <h5 class='section'>See Also:</h5><ul>
705       *    <li class='ja'>{@link BeanConfig#beanFieldVisibility()}
706       * </ul>
707       *
708       * @param value
709       *    The new value for this setting.
710       *    <br>The default is {@link Visibility#PUBLIC}.
711       *    <br>Cannot be <jk>null</jk>.
712       * @return This object.
713       */
714      public Builder beanFieldVisibility(Visibility value) {
715         beanFieldVisibility = reqnn("value", value);
716         return this;
717      }

719      /**
720       * Bean interceptor.
721       *
722       * <p>
723       * Bean interceptors can be used to intercept calls to getters and setters and alter their values in transit.
724       *
725       * <h5 class='section'>Example:</h5>
726       * <p class='bjava'>
727       *    <jc>// Interceptor that strips out sensitive information.</jc>
728       *    <jk>public class</jk> AddressInterceptor <jk>extends</jk> BeanInterceptor&lt;Address&gt; {
729       *
730       *       <jk>public</jk> Object readProperty(Address <jv>bean</jv>, String <jv>name</jv>, Object <jv>value</jv>) {
731       *          <jk>if</jk> (<js>"taxInfo"</js>.equals(<jv>name</jv>))
732       *             <jk>return</jk> <js>"redacted"</js>;
733       *          <jk>return</jk> <jv>value</jv>;
734       *       }
735       *
736       *       <jk>public</jk> Object writeProperty(Address <jv>bean</jv>, String <jv>name</jv>, Object <jv>value</jv>) {
737       *          <jk>if</jk> (<js>"taxInfo"</js>.equals(<jv>name</jv>) &amp;&amp; <js>"redacted"</js>.equals(<jv>value</jv>))
738       *             <jk>return</jk> TaxInfoUtils.<jsm>lookup</jsm>(<jv>bean</jv>.getStreet(), <jv>bean</jv>.getCity(), <jv>bean</jv>.getState());
739       *          <jk>return</jk> <jv>value</jv>;
740       *       }
741       *    }
742       *
743       *    <jc>// Our bean class.</jc>
744       *    <jk>public class</jk> Address {
745       *       <jk>public</jk> String getTaxInfo() {...}
746       *       <jk>public void</jk> setTaxInfo(String <jv>value</jv>) {...}
747       *    }
748       *
749       *    <jc>// Register filter on serializer or parser.</jc>
750       *    WriterSerializer <jv>serializer</jv> = JsonSerializer
751       *       .<jsm>create</jsm>()
752       *       .beanInterceptor(Address.<jk>class</jk>, AddressInterceptor.<jk>class</jk>)
753       *       .build();
754       *
755       *    <jc>// Produces:  {"taxInfo":"redacted"}</jc>
756       *    String <jv>json</jv> = <jv>serializer</jv>.write(<jk>new</jk> Address());
757       * </p>
758       *
759       * <h5 class='section'>See Also:</h5><ul>
760       *    <li class='jc'>{@link BeanInterceptor}
761       *    <li class='ja'>{@link Marshalled#interceptor() @Marshalled(interceptor)}
762       * </ul>
763       *
764       * @param on The bean that the filter applies to.
765       *    <br>Cannot be <jk>null</jk>.
766       * @param value
767       *    The new value for this setting.
768       *    <br>Cannot be <jk>null</jk>.
769       * @return This object.
770       */
771      public Builder beanInterceptor(Class<?> on, Class<? extends BeanInterceptor<?>> value) {
772         reqnn("on", on);
773         reqnn("value", value);
774         return annotations(MarshalledApplyAnnotation.create(on).value(MarshalledAnnotation.create().interceptor(value).build()).build());
775      }

777      /**
778       * BeanMap.put() returns old property value.
779       *
780       * <p>
781       * When enabled, then the {@link BeanMap#put(String,Object) BeanMap.put()} method will return old property
782       * values.  Otherwise, it returns <jk>null</jk>.
783       *
784       * <p>
785       * Disabled by default because it introduces a slight performance penalty during serialization.
786       *
787       * <h5 class='section'>Example:</h5>

792       *       .beanMapPutReturnsOldValue()
793       *       .build();

796       *    <jv>myBeanMap</jv>.put(<js>"foo"</js>, <js>"bar"</js>);
797       *    Object <jv>oldValue</jv> = <jv>myBeanMap</jv>.put(<js>"foo"</js>, <js>"baz"</js>);  <jc>// oldValue == "bar"</jc>
798       * </p>
799       *
800       * <h5 class='section'>See Also:</h5><ul>
801       *    <li class='ja'>{@link BeanConfig#beanMapPutReturnsOldValue()}
802       * </ul>
803       *
804       * @return This object.
805       */
806      public Builder beanMapPutReturnsOldValue() {
807         return beanMapPutReturnsOldValue(true);
808      }

821      /**

826       *
827       * <p>
828       * This affects which methods are detected as getters and setters on a bean class. Normally only <jk>public</jk> getters and setters are considered.
829       * Use this setting if you want to reduce the visibility requirement.

831       * <h5 class='section'>Example:</h5>

848       *
849       * <h5 class='section'>Notes:</h5><ul>
850       *    <li class='note'>The {@link BeanProp @BeanProp} annotation can also be used to expose a non-public method.
851       *    <li class='note'>The {@link BeanIgnore @BeanIgnore} annotation can also be used on a public bean getter/setter to ignore it as a bean property.
852       * </ul>

868      /**
869       * Bean property includes.
870       *
871       * <p>
872       * Specifies the set and order of names of properties associated with the bean class.
873       *
874       * <p>
875       * For example, <c>beanProperties(MyBean.<jk>class</jk>, <js>"foo,bar"</js>)</c> means only serialize the <c>foo</c> and
876       * <c>bar</c> properties on the specified bean.  Likewise, parsing will ignore any bean properties not specified
877       * and either throw an exception or silently ignore them depending on whether {@link #ignoreUnknownBeanProperties()}
878       * has been called.
879       *
880       * <p>
881       * This value is entirely optional if you simply want to expose all the getters and public fields on
882       * a class as bean properties.  However, it's useful if you want certain getters to be ignored or you want the properties to be
883       * serialized in a particular order.  Note that on IBM JREs, the property order is the same as the order in the source code,
884       * whereas on Oracle JREs, the order is entirely random.
885       *
886       * <p>
887       * Setting applies to specified class and all subclasses.
888       *
889       * <h5 class='section'>Example:</h5>
890       * <p class='bjava'>
891       *    <jc>// A bean with 3 properties.</jc>
892       *    <jk>public class</jk> MyBean {
893       *       <jk>public</jk> String
894       *          <jf>foo</jf> = <js>"foo"</js>,
895       *          <jf>bar</jf> = <js>"bar"</js>,
896       *          <jf>baz</jf> = <js>"baz"</js>;
897       *    }
898       *
899       *    <jc>// Create a serializer that includes only the 'foo' and 'bar' properties on the MyBean class.</jc>
900       *    WriterSerializer <jv>serializer</jv> = JsonSerializer
901       *       .<jsm>create</jsm>()
902       *       .beanProperties(MyBean.<jk>class</jk>, <js>"foo,bar"</js>)
903       *       .build();
904       *
905       *    <jc>// Produces:  {"foo":"foo","bar":"bar"}</jc>
906       *    String <jv>json</jv> = <jv>serializer</jv>.write(<jk>new</jk> MyBean());
907       * </p>
908       *
909       * <p>
910       * This method is functionally equivalent to the following code:
911       * <p class='bjava'>
912       *    <jv>builder</jv>.annotations(MarshalledAnnotation.<jsm>create</jsm>(<jv>beanClass</jv>).properties(<jv>properties</jv>).build());
913       * </p>
914       *
915       * <h5 class='section'>See Also:</h5><ul>
916       *    <li class='jma'>{@link BeanType#properties()}/{@link BeanType#p()} - On an annotation on the bean class itself.
917       * </ul>
918       *
919       * @param beanClass The bean class.
920       *    <br>Cannot be <jk>null</jk>.
921       * @param properties Comma-delimited list of property names.
922       *    <br>Cannot be <jk>null</jk>.
923       * @return This object.
924       */
925      public Builder beanProperties(Class<?> beanClass, String properties) {
926         reqnn("beanClass", beanClass);
927         reqnn("properties", properties);
928         return annotations(BeanTypeApplyAnnotation.create(beanClass).value(BeanTypeAnnotation.create().p(properties).build()).build());
929      }

931      /**
932       * Bean property includes.
933       *
934       * <p>
935       * Specifies the set and order of names of properties associated with bean classes.
936       *
937       * <p>
938       * For example, <c>beanProperties(AMap.<jsm>of</jsm>(<js>"MyBean"</js>, <js>"foo,bar"</js>))</c> means only serialize the <c>foo</c> and
939       * <c>bar</c> properties on the specified bean.  Likewise, parsing will ignore any bean properties not specified
940       * and either throw an exception or silently ignore them depending on whether {@link #ignoreUnknownBeanProperties()}
941       * has been called.
942       *
943       * <p>
944       * This value is entirely optional if you simply want to expose all the getters and public fields on
945       * a class as bean properties.  However, it's useful if you want certain getters to be ignored or you want the properties to be
946       * serialized in a particular order.  Note that on IBM JREs, the property order is the same as the order in the source code,
947       * whereas on Oracle JREs, the order is entirely random.
948       *
949       * <p>
950       * Setting applies to specified class and all subclasses.
951       *
952       * <h5 class='section'>Example:</h5>
953       * <p class='bjava'>
954       *    <jc>// A bean with 3 properties.</jc>
955       *    <jk>public class</jk> MyBean {
956       *       <jk>public</jk> String
957       *          <jf>foo</jf> = <js>"foo"</js>,
958       *          <jf>bar</jf> = <js>"bar"</js>,
959       *          <jf>baz</jf> = <js>"baz"</js>;
960       *    }
961       *
962       *    <jc>// Create a serializer that includes only the 'foo' and 'bar' properties on the MyBean class.</jc>
963       *    WriterSerializer <jv>serializer</jv> = JsonSerializer
964       *       .<jsm>create</jsm>()
965       *       .beanProperties(AMap.<jsm>of</jsm>(<js>"MyBean"</js>, <js>"foo,bar"</js>))
966       *       .build();
967       *
968       *    <jc>// Produces:  {"foo":"foo","bar":"bar"}</jc>
969       *    String <jv>json</jv> = <jv>serializer</jv>.write(<jk>new</jk> MyBean());
970       * </p>
971       *
972       * <p>
973       * This method is functionally equivalent to the following code for each entry:
974       * <p class='bjava'>
975       *    <jv>builder</jv>.annotations(MarshalledAnnotation.<jsm>create</jsm>(<jv>key</jv>).properties(<jv>value</jv>.toString()).build());
976       * </p>
977       *
978       * <h5 class='section'>See Also:</h5><ul>
979       *    <li class='jma'>{@link BeanType#properties()} / {@link BeanType#p()}- On an annotation on the bean class itself.
980       * </ul>
981       *
982       * @param values
983       *    The values to add to this builder.
984       *    <br>Keys are bean class names which can be a simple name, fully-qualified name, or <js>"*"</js> for all beans.
985       *    <br>Values are comma-delimited lists of property names.  Non-String objects are first converted to Strings.
986       *    <br>Cannot be <jk>null</jk>.
987       * @return This object.
988       */
989      public Builder beanProperties(Map<String,Object> values) {
990         reqnn("values", values);
991         values.forEach((k, v) -> annotations(BeanTypeApplyAnnotation.create(k).value(BeanTypeAnnotation.create().p(s(v)).build()).build()));
992         return this;
993      }

995      /**
996       * Bean property includes.
997       *
998       * <p>
999       * Specifies the set and order of names of properties associated with the bean class.
1000       *
1001       * <p>
1002       * For example, <c>beanProperties(<js>"MyBean"</js>, <js>"foo,bar"</js>)</c> means only serialize the <c>foo</c> and
1003       * <c>bar</c> properties on the specified bean.  Likewise, parsing will ignore any bean properties not specified
1004       * and either throw an exception or silently ignore them depending on whether {@link #ignoreUnknownBeanProperties()}
1005       * has been called.
1006       *
1007       * <p>
1008       * This value is entirely optional if you simply want to expose all the getters and public fields on
1009       * a class as bean properties.  However, it's useful if you want certain getters to be ignored or you want the properties to be
1010       * serialized in a particular order.  Note that on IBM JREs, the property order is the same as the order in the source code,
1011       * whereas on Oracle JREs, the order is entirely random.
1012       *
1013       * <p>
1014       * Setting applies to specified class and all subclasses.
1015       *
1016       * <h5 class='section'>Example:</h5>
1017       * <p class='bjava'>
1018       *    <jc>// A bean with 3 properties.</jc>
1019       *    <jk>public class</jk> MyBean {
1020       *       <jk>public</jk> String
1021       *          <jf>foo</jf> = <js>"foo"</js>,
1022       *          <jf>bar</jf> = <js>"bar"</js>,
1023       *          <jf>baz</jf> = <js>"baz"</js>;
1024       *    }
1025       *
1026       *    <jc>// Create a serializer that includes only the 'foo' and 'bar' properties on the MyBean class.</jc>
1027       *    WriterSerializer <jv>serializer</jv> = JsonSerializer
1028       *       .<jsm>create</jsm>()
1029       *       .beanProperties(<js>"MyBean"</js>, <js>"foo,bar"</js>)
1030       *       .build();
1031       *
1032       *    <jc>// Produces:  {"foo":"foo","bar":"bar"}</jc>
1033       *    String <jv>json</jv> = <jv>serializer</jv>.write(<jk>new</jk> MyBean());
1034       * </p>
1035       *
1036       * <p>
1037       * This method is functionally equivalent to the following code:
1038       * <p class='bjava'>
1039       *    <jv>builder</jv>.annotations(MarshalledAnnotation.<jsm>create</jsm>(<jv>beanClassName</jv>).properties(<jv>properties</jv>).build());
1040       * </p>
1041       *
1042       * <h5 class='section'>See Also:</h5><ul>
1043       *    <li class='jma'>{@link BeanType#properties()} / {@link BeanType#p()} - On an annotation on the bean class itself.
1044       * </ul>

1522       * Parsers will parse such properties as usual, but serializers will silently ignore them.
1523       * Note that this is different from the {@link #beanProperties(Class,String) beanProperties}/{@link #beanPropertiesExcludes(Class,String) beanPropertiesExcludes} settings which include or exclude properties
1524       * for both serializers and parsers.
1525       *
1526       * <h5 class='section'>Example:</h5>
1527       * <p class='bjava'>
1528       *    <jc>// A bean with 3 properties.</jc>
1529       *    <jk>public class</jk> MyBean {
1530       *       <jk>public</jk> String <jf>foo</jf>, <jf>bar</jf>, <jf>baz</jf>;
1531       *    }
1532       *
1533       *    <jc>// Create a serializer with write-only property settings.</jc>
1534       *    WriterSerializer <jv>serializer</jv> = JsonSerializer
1535       *       .<jsm>create</jsm>()
1536       *       .beanPropertiesWriteOnly(<js>"MyBean"</js>, <js>"bar,baz"</js>)
1537       *       .build();
1538       *
1539       *    <jc>// Only foo will be serialized.</jc>
1540       *    String <jv>json</jv> = <jv>serializer</jv>.write(<jk>new</jk> MyBean());
1541       *
1542       *    <jc>// Create a parser with write-only property settings.</jc>
1543       *    ReaderParser <jv>parser</jv> = JsonParser
1544       *       .<jsm>create</jsm>()
1545       *       .beanPropertiesWriteOnly(<js>"MyBean"</js>, <js>"bar,baz"</js>)
1546       *       .build();
1547       *
1548       *    <jc>// Parser parses all 3 properties.</jc>
1549       *    MyBean <jv>myBean</jv> = <jv>parser</jv>.read(<js>"{foo:'foo',bar:'bar',baz:'baz'}"</js>, MyBean.<jk>class</jk>);
1550       * </p>
1551       *
1552       * <p>
1553       * This method is functionally equivalent to the following code:
1554       * <p class='bjava'>
1555       *    <jv>builder</jv>.annotations(MarshalledAnnotation.<jsm>create</jsm>(<jv>beanClassName</jv>).writeOnlyProperties(<jv>properties</jv>).build());
1556       * </p>
1557       *
1558       * <h5 class='section'>See Also:</h5><ul>
1559       *    <li class='jma'>{@link BeanType#writeOnlyProperties()} / {@link BeanType#wo()}
1560       * </ul>
1561       *
1562       * @param beanClassName
1563       *    The bean class name.
1564       *    <br>Can be a simple name, fully-qualified name, or <js>"*"</js> for all bean classes.
1565       * @param properties Comma-delimited list of property names.
1566       * @return This object.
1567       */
1568      public Builder beanPropertiesWriteOnly(String beanClassName, String properties) {
1569         reqnn("beanClassName", beanClassName);
1570         reqnn("properties", properties);
1571         return annotations(BeanTypeApplyAnnotation.create(beanClassName).value(BeanTypeAnnotation.create().wo(properties).build()).build());
1572      }
1573
1574      /**
1575       * Beans require no-arg constructors.
1576       *
1577       * <p>
1578       * When enabled, a Java class must implement a default no-arg constructor to be considered a bean.
1579       * Otherwise, the bean will be serialized as a string using the {@link Object#toString()} method.
1580       *
1581       * <h5 class='section'>Example:</h5>
1582       * <p class='bjava'>
1583       *    <jc>// A bean without a no-arg constructor.</jc>
1584       *    <jk>public class</jk> MyBean {
1585       *
1586       *       <jc>// A property method.</jc>
1587       *       <jk>public</jk> String <jf>foo</jf> = <js>"bar"</js>;
1588       *
1589       *       <jc>// A no-arg constructor</jc>
1590       *       <jk>public</jk> MyBean(String <jv>foo</jv>) {
1591       *          <jk>this</jk>.<jf>foo</jf> = <jv>foo</jv>;
1592       *       }
1593       *
1594       *       <ja>@Override</ja>
1595       *       <jk>public</jk> String toString() {
1596       *          <jk>return</jk> <js>"bar"</js>;
1597       *       }
1598       *    }
1599       *
1600       *    <jc>// Create a serializer that ignores beans without default constructors.</jc>
1601       *    WriterSerializer <jv>serializer</jv> = JsonSerializer
1602       *       .<jsm>create</jsm>()
1603       *       .beansRequireDefaultConstructor()
1604       *       .build();
1605       *
1606       *    <jc>// Produces:  "bar"</jc>
1607       *    String <jv>json</jv> = <jv>serializer</jv>.write(<jk>new</jk> MyBean());
1608       * </p>
1609       *
1610       * <h5 class='section'>Notes:</h5><ul>
1611       *    <li class='note'>The {@link Bean @Marshalled} annotation can be used on a bean class to override this setting.
1612       *    <li class='note'>The {@link BeanIgnore @BeanIgnore} annotation can also be used on a class to ignore it as a bean.
1613       * </ul>
1614       *
1615       * <h5 class='section'>See Also:</h5><ul>
1616       *    <li class='ja'>{@link BeanConfig#beansRequireDefaultConstructor()}
1617       * </ul>
1618       *
1619       * @return This object.
1620       */
1621      public Builder beansRequireDefaultConstructor() {
1622         return beansRequireDefaultConstructor(true);
1623      }
1624
1625      /**
1626       * Same as {@link #beansRequireDefaultConstructor()} but allows you to explicitly specify the value.
1627       *
1628       * @param value The value for this setting.
1629       * @return This object.
1630       */
1631      public Builder beansRequireDefaultConstructor(boolean value) {
1632         beansRequireDefaultConstructor = value;
1633         return this;
1634      }

1639       * <p>

1641       * Otherwise, the bean will be serialized as a string using the {@link Object#toString()} method.

1648       *       <jc>// A property method.</jc>

1651       *       <ja>@Override</ja>

1654       *       }
1655       *    }

1658       *    WriterSerializer <jv>serializer</jv> = JsonSerializer
1659       *       .<jsm>create</jsm>()

1661       *       .build();

1670       * </ul>
1671       *
1672       * <h5 class='section'>See Also:</h5><ul>
1673       *    <li class='ja'>{@link BeanConfig#beansRequireSerializable()}
1674       * </ul>
1675       *
1676       * @return This object.
1677       */
1678      public Builder beansRequireSerializable() {
1679         return beansRequireSerializable(true);

1693      /**
1694       * Beans require setters for getters.
1695       *
1696       * <p>
1697       * When enabled, ignore read-only properties (properties with getters but not setters).
1698       *
1699       * <h5 class='section'>Example:</h5>
1700       * <p class='bjava'>
1701       *    <jc>// A bean without a Serializable interface.</jc>
1702       *    <jk>public class</jk> MyBean {
1703       *
1704       *       <jc>// A read/write property.</jc>
1705       *       <jk>public</jk> String getFoo() { <jk>return</jk> <js>"foo"</js>; }
1706       *       <jk>public void</jk> setFoo(String <jv>foo</jv>) { ... }
1707       *
1708       *       <jc>// A read-only property.</jc>
1709       *       <jk>public</jk> String getBar() { <jk>return</jk> <js>"bar"</js>; }
1710       *    }
1711       *
1712       *    <jc>// Create a serializer that ignores bean properties without setters.</jc>
1713       *    WriterSerializer <jv>serializer</jv> = JsonSerializer
1714       *       .<jsm>create</jsm>()
1715       *       .beansRequireSettersForGetters()
1716       *       .build();
1717       *
1718       *    <jc>// Produces:  {"foo":"foo"}</jc>
1719       *    String <jv>json</jv> = <jv>serializer</jv>.write(<jk>new</jk> MyBean());
1720       * </p>
1721       *
1722       * <h5 class='section'>Notes:</h5><ul>
1723       *    <li class='note'>The {@link BeanProp @BeanProp} annotation can be used on the getter to override this setting.
1724       *    <li class='note'>The {@link BeanIgnore @BeanIgnore} annotation can also be used on getters to ignore them as bean properties.
1725       * </ul>
1726       *
1727       * @return This object.
1728       */
1729      public Builder beansRequireSettersForGetters() {
1730         return beansRequireSettersForGetters(true);
1731      }

1738       */
1739      public Builder beansRequireSettersForGetters(boolean value) {

1741         return this;

1744      /**
1745       * Sets the bean store used for factory-based instantiation.
1746       *
1747       * <p>
1748       * The bean store is used to resolve {@link BeanFactory} instances registered via
1749       * <ja>@BeanType</ja><c>(factory=X.class)</c> and <ja>@BeanProp</ja><c>(factory=X.class)</c> annotations.
1750       * When a factory class is encountered, the framework first looks it up in the bean store
1751       * before attempting direct instantiation.
1752       *
1753       * <p>
1754       * Typically set to a {@code SpringBeanStore} wrapping the application's
1755       * {@code ApplicationContext} so that Spring-managed factories are resolved automatically.
1756       *
1757       * <h5 class='section'>Example:</h5>
1758       * <p class='bjava'>
1759       *    <jk>public class</jk> MyRestServlet <jk>extends</jk> BasicRestServlet {
1760       *       <ja>@Autowired</ja> ApplicationContext <jv>ctx</jv>;
1761       *
1762       *       <ja>@Override</ja>
1763       *       <jk>protected</jk> MarshallingContext createBeanContext(MarshallingContext.Builder<?> <jv>builder</jv>) {
1764       *          <jk>return</jk> <jv>builder</jv>.beanStore(<jk>new</jk> SpringBeanStore(<jv>ctx</jv>)).build();
1765       *       }
1766       *    }
1767       * </p>
1768       *
1769       * @param value The bean store, or <jk>null</jk> to use direct instantiation only.
1770       * @return This object.
1771       */
1772      public Builder beanStore(BeanStore value) {
1773         beanStore = value;
1774         return this;
1775      }
1776
1777      @Override /* Overridden from Context.Builder<?> */
1778      public MarshallingContext build() {
1779         return cache(CACHE).build(MarshallingContext.class);
1780      }
1781
1782      @Override /* Overridden from Context.Builder<?> */
1783      public Builder copy() {
1784         return new Builder(this);
1785      }

1787      /**
1788       * Null-safe copy: returns a deep copy of the specified value, or <jk>null</jk> if the value is <jk>null</jk>.
1789       *
1790    * @param value The value to copy.  Can be <jk>null</jk> (returns <jk>null</jk>).
1791    * @return A copy of the value, or <jk>null</jk> if the value was <jk>null</jk>.
1792       */
1793      public static Builder copyOrNull(Builder value) {
1794         return value == null ? null : value.copy();
1795      }

1797      /**
1798       * Bean dictionary.
1799       *
1800       * <p>
1801       * This is identical to {@link #beanDictionary(Class...)}, but specifies a dictionary within the context of
1802       * a single class as opposed to globally.
1803       *
1804       * <h5 class='section'>Example:</h5>
1805       * <p class='bjava'>
1806       *    <jc>// POJOs with @Marshalled(name) annotations.</jc>
1807       *    <ja>@Marshalled</ja>(typeName=<js>"foo"</js>)
1808       *    <jk>public class</jk> Foo {...}
1809       *    <ja>@Marshalled</ja>(typeName=<js>"bar"</js>)
1810       *    <jk>public class</jk> Bar {...}
1811       *
1812       *    <jc>// A bean with a field with an indeterminate type.</jc>
1813       *    <jk>public class</jk> MyBean {
1814       *       <jk>public</jk> Object <jf>mySimpleField</jf>;
1815       *    }
1816       *
1817       *    <jc>// Create a parser and tell it which classes to try to resolve.</jc>
1818       *    ReaderParser <jv>parser</jv> = JsonParser
1819       *       .<jsm>create</jsm>()
1820       *       .dictionaryOn(MyBean.<jk>class</jk>, Foo.<jk>class</jk>, Bar.<jk>class</jk>)
1821       *       .build();
1822       *
1823       *    <jc>// Parse bean.</jc>
1824       *    MyBean <jv>myBean</jv> = <jv>parser</jv>.read(<js>"{mySimpleField:{_type:'foo',...}}"</js>, MyBean.<jk>class</jk>);
1825       * </p>
1826       *
1827       * <p>
1828       * This is functionally equivalent to the {@link Marshalled#dictionary()} annotation.
1829       *
1830       * <h5 class='section'>See Also:</h5><ul>
1831       *    <li class='jma'>{@link Marshalled#dictionary()}
1832       *    <li class='jm'>{@link #beanDictionary(Class...)}
1833       * </ul>
1834       *
1835       * @param on The class that the dictionary values apply to.
1836       * @param values
1837       *    The new values for this setting.
1838       * @return This object.
1839       */
1840      public Builder dictionaryOn(Class<?> on, Class<?>...values) {
1841         reqnn("on", on);
1842         reqnns("values", values);
1843         return annotations(MarshalledApplyAnnotation.create(on).value(MarshalledAnnotation.create().dictionary(values).build()).build());
1844      }

1846      /**
1847       * Beans don't require at least one property.
1848       *
1849       * <p>
1850       * When enabled, then a Java class doesn't need to contain at least 1 property to be considered a bean.
1851       * Otherwise, the bean will be serialized as a string using the {@link Object#toString()} method.
1852       *
1853       * <p>
1854       * The {@link Bean @Marshalled} annotation can be used on a class to override this setting when <jk>true</jk>.
1855       *
1856       * <h5 class='section'>Example:</h5>
1857       * <p class='bjava'>
1858       *    <jc>// A bean with no properties.</jc>
1859       *    <jk>public class</jk> MyBean {
1860       *    }
1861       *
1862       *    <jc>// Create a serializer that serializes beans even if they have zero properties.</jc>
1863       *    WriterSerializer <jv>serializer</jv> = JsonSerializer
1864       *       .<jsm>create</jsm>()
1865       *       .disableBeansRequireSomeProperties()
1866       *       .build();
1867       *
1868       *    <jc>// Produces:  {}</jc>
1869       *    String <jv>json</jv> = <jv>serializer</jv>.write(<jk>new</jk> MyBean());
1870       * </p>
1871       *
1872       * <h5 class='section'>Notes:</h5><ul>
1873       *    <li class='note'>The {@link Bean @Marshalled} annotation can be used on the class to force it to be recognized as a bean class
1874       *       even if it has no properties.
1875       * </ul>
1876       *
1877       * <h5 class='section'>See Also:</h5><ul>
1878       *    <li class='ja'>{@link BeanConfig#disableBeansRequireSomeProperties()}
1879       * </ul>
1880       *
1881       * @return This object.
1882       */
1883      public Builder disableBeansRequireSomeProperties() {

1896      }

1898      /**
1899       * Don't silently ignore missing setters.
1900       *
1901       * <p>
1902       * When enabled, trying to set a value on a bean property without a setter will throw a {@link BeanRuntimeException}.
1903       * Otherwise, it will be silently ignored.
1904       *
1905       * <h5 class='section'>Example:</h5>
1906       * <p class='bjava'>
1907       *    <jc>// A bean with a property with a getter but not a setter.</jc>
1908       *    <jk>public class</jk> MyBean {
1909       *       <jk>public void</jk> getFoo() {
1910       *          <jk>return</jk> <js>"foo"</js>;
1911       *       }
1912       *    }

1914       *    <jc>// Create a parser that throws an exception if a setter is not found but a getter is.</jc>

1916       *       .<jsm>create</jsm>()
1917       *       .disableIgnoreMissingSetters()
1918       *       .build();

1920       *    <jc>// Throws a ParseException.</jc>
1921       *    MyBean <jv>myBean</jv> = <jv>parser</jv>.read(<js>"{foo:'bar'}"</js>, MyBean.<jk>class</jk>);
1922       * </p>
1923       *
1924       * <h5 class='section'>Notes:</h5><ul>
1925       *    <li class='note'>The {@link BeanIgnore @BeanIgnore} annotation can also be used on getters and fields to ignore them.
1926       * </ul>

1928       * <h5 class='section'>See Also:</h5><ul>
1929       *    <li class='ja'>{@link BeanConfig#disableIgnoreMissingSetters()}
1930       * </ul>

1932       * @return This object.
1933       */

1935         return disableIgnoreMissingSetters(true);
1936      }

1946         return this;
1947      }

2083       * <h5 class='section'>Example:</h5>
2084       * <p class='bjava'>
2085       *    <jc>// Create a serializer that excludes the 'foo' and 'bar' properties on the MyBean class.</jc>
2086       *    WriterSerializer <jv>serializer</jv> = JsonSerializer
2087       *       .<jsm>create</jsm>()
2088       *       .example(MyBean.<jk>class</jk>, <js>"{foo:'bar'}"</js>)
2089       *       .build();
2090       * </p>
2091       *
2092       * <p>
2093       * This is a shorthand method for the following code:
2094       * <p class='bjava'>
2095       *    <jv>builder</jv>.annotations(MarshalledAnnotation.<jsm>create</jsm>(<jv>pojoClass</jv>).example(<jv>json</jv>).build())
2096       * </p>
2097       *
2098       * <p>
2099       * POJO examples can also be defined on classes via the following:
2100       * <ul class='spaced-list'>
2101       *    <li>A static field annotated with {@link Example @Example}.
2102       *    <li>A static method annotated with {@link Example @Example} with zero arguments or one {@link MarshallingSession} argument.
2103       *    <li>A static method with name <c>example</c> with no arguments or one {@link MarshallingSession} argument.
2104       * </ul>
2105       *
2106       * <h5 class='section'>See Also:</h5><ul>
2107       *    <li class='ja'>{@link Marshalled#example()}
2108       * </ul>
2109       *
2110       * @param <T> The POJO class type.
2111       * @param pojoClass The POJO class.
2112       *    <br>Cannot be <jk>null</jk>.
2113       * @param json The JSON 5 representation of the example.
2114       *    <br>Can be <jk>null</jk> or empty (treated as no example).
2115       * @return This object.
2116       */
2117      public <T> Builder example(Class<T> pojoClass, String json) {
2118         return annotations(MarshalledApplyAnnotation.create(reqnn("pojoClass", pojoClass)).value(MarshalledAnnotation.create().example(json).build()).build());
2119      }

2121      /**
2122       * POJO example.
2123       *
2124       * <p>
2125       * Specifies an example of the specified class.
2126       *
2127       * <p>
2128       * Examples are used in cases such as POJO examples in Swagger documents.
2129       *
2130       * <h5 class='section'>Example:</h5>
2131       * <p class='bjava'>
2132       *    <jc>// Create a serializer that excludes the 'foo' and 'bar' properties on the MyBean class.</jc>
2133       *    WriterSerializer <jv>serializer</jv> = JsonSerializer
2134       *       .<jsm>create</jsm>()
2135       *       .example(MyBean.<jk>class</jk>, <jk>new</jk> MyBean().setFoo(<js>"foo"</js>).setBar(123))
2136       *       .build();
2137       * </p>
2138       *
2139       * <p>
2140       * This is a shorthand method for the following code:
2141       * <p class='bjava'>
2142       *       <jv>builder</jv>.annotations(MarshalledAnnotation.<jsm>create</jsm>(<jv>pojoClass</jv>).example(Json5.<jsf>DEFAULT</jsf>.toString(<jv>object</jv>)).build())
2143       * </p>
2144       *
2145       * <h5 class='section'>Notes:</h5><ul>
2146       *    <li class='note'>Using this method assumes the serialized form of the object is the same as that produced
2147       *       by the default serializer.  This may not be true based on settings or swaps on the constructed serializer.
2148       * </ul>
2149       *
2150       * <p>
2151       * POJO examples can also be defined on classes via the following:
2152       * <ul class='spaced-list'>
2153       *    <li>The {@link Marshalled#example()} annotation on the class itself.
2154       *    <li>A static field annotated with {@link Example @Example}.
2155       *    <li>A static method annotated with {@link Example @Example} with zero arguments or one {@link MarshallingSession} argument.
2156       *    <li>A static method with name <c>example</c> with no arguments or one {@link MarshallingSession} argument.
2157       * </ul>
2158       *
2159       * @param <T> The POJO class.
2160       * @param pojoClass The POJO class.
2161       *    <br>Cannot be <jk>null</jk>.
2162       * @param o
2163       *    An instance of the POJO class used for examples.
2164       *    <br>Can be <jk>null</jk> (will be serialized as <js>"null"</js>).
2165       * @return This object.
2166       */
2167      public <T> Builder example(Class<T> pojoClass, T o) {
2168         return annotations(MarshalledApplyAnnotation.create(reqnn("pojoClass", pojoClass)).value(MarshalledAnnotation.create().example(Json5.of(o)).build()).build());
2169      }

2171      /**
2172       * Find fluent setters.
2173       *
2174       * <p>
2175       * When enabled, fluent setters are detected on beans during parsing.
2176       *
2177       * <p>
2178       * Fluent setters must have the following attributes:
2179       * <ul>
2180       *    <li>Public.
2181       *    <li>Not static.
2182       *    <li>Take in one parameter.
2183       *    <li>Return the bean itself.
2184       * </ul>
2185       *
2186       * <h5 class='section'>Example:</h5>
2187       * <p class='bjava'>
2188       *    <jc>// A bean with a fluent setter.</jc>
2189       *    <jk>public class</jk> MyBean {
2190       *       <jk>public</jk> MyBean foo(String <jv>value</jv>) {...}
2191       *    }
2192       *
2193       *    <jc>// Create a parser that finds fluent setters.</jc>
2194       *    ReaderParser <jv>parser</jv> = JsonParser
2195       *       .<jsm>create</jsm>()
2196       *       .findFluentSetters()
2197       *       .build();
2198       *
2199       *    <jc>// Parse into bean using fluent setter.</jc>
2200       *    MyBean <jv>myBean</jv> = <jv>parser</jv>.read(<js>"{foo:'bar'}"</js>);
2201       * </p>
2202       *
2203       * <h5 class='section'>Notes:</h5><ul>
2204       *    <li class='note'>The {@link BeanProp @BeanProp} annotation can also be used on methods to individually identify them as fluent setters.
2205       *    <li class='note'>The {@link BeanType#findFluentSetters() @BeanType.findFluentSetters()} annotation can also be used on classes to specify to look for fluent setters.
2206       * </ul>
2207       *
2208       * <h5 class='section'>See Also:</h5><ul>
2209       *    <li class='ja'>{@link BeanType#findFluentSetters()}
2210       *    <li class='ja'>{@link BeanConfig#findFluentSetters()}
2211       * </ul>
2212       *
2213       * @return This object.
2214       */
2215      public Builder findFluentSetters() {
2216         return findFluentSetters(true);
2217      }

2219      /**

2224       */

2227         return this;
2228      }

2230      /**
2231       * Find fluent setters.
2232       *

2245       *       .<jsm>create</jsm>()

2248       *
2249       *    <jc>// Parse into bean using fluent setter.</jc>
2250       *    MyBean <jv>myBean</jv> = <jv>parser</jv>.read(<js>"{foo:'bar'}"</js>);

2252       *
2253       * <h5 class='section'>Notes:</h5><ul>

2333      /**
2334       * Sets the default active view name for all sessions created from this context.
2335       *
2336       * <p>
2337       * When set, only bean properties whose declared {@link MarshalledProp#view()} set contains this view name
2338       * will be included during serialization.  On the parse side, properties outside the active view are routed
2339       * through the existing unknown/ignored-property mechanism governed by
2340       * {@link #ignoreUnknownBeanProperties()}.
2341       *
2342       * <p>
2343       * Untagged properties (those whose declared view set is empty) follow the default-view-inclusion policy:
2344       * included under every active view unless {@link #disableDefaultViewInclusion()} has been called.
2345       *
2346       * <p>
2347       * This value can be overridden per serialization or parse call via the session builder (e.g.
2348       * {@link MarshallingSession.Builder#activeView(String)}).
2349       *
2350       * <h5 class='section'>Example:</h5>
2351       * <p class='bjava'>
2352       *    JsonSerializer <jv>serializer</jv> = JsonSerializer.<jsm>create</jsm>()
2353       *       .activeView(<js>"summary"</js>)
2354       *       .build();
2355       * </p>
2356       *
2357       * <h5 class='section'>See Also:</h5><ul>
2358       *    <li class='ja'>{@link MarshalledProp#view()}
2359       *    <li class='jm'>{@link MarshallingSession.Builder#activeView(String)}
2360       * </ul>
2361       *
2362       * @param value The active view name.  Use <jk>null</jk> to disable view filtering.
2363       * @return This object.
2364       * @since 10.0.0
2365       */
2366      public Builder activeView(String value) {
2367         activeView = value;
2368         return this;
2369      }

2543      /**
2544       * Schema validation mode.
2545       *
2546       * <p>
2547       * When enabled, bean property values are validated against the constraints declared by
2548       * {@link Schema @Schema} annotations on those properties.  Validation runs
2549       * during both <b>parsing</b> (value set on the bean) and <b>serialization</b> (value read from the bean).
2550       *
2551       * <p>
2552       * Backed by the typed {@code JsonSchema} bean in {@code juneau-bean-jsonschema} and JSON Schema Draft 2020-12
2553       * semantics.  Validation failures throw {@link SchemaValidationException}
2554       * wrapped in {@code BeanRuntimeException}; the parser surfaces them as
2555       * {@link ParseException} and the serializer surfaces them as
2556       * {@link SerializeException}.
2557       *
2558       * <p>
2559       * If {@code juneau-bean-jsonschema} is not on the classpath, this flag becomes a silent no-op.
2560       *
2561       * <h5 class='section'>Example:</h5>
2562       * <p class='bjava'>
2563       *    <jc>// A bean with a length-constrained property.</jc>
2564       *    <jk>public class</jk> MyBean {
2565       *       <ja>&#64;Schema</ja>(minLength=<js>"2"</js>, maxLength=<js>"10"</js>)
2566       *       <jk>public</jk> String <jf>name</jf>;
2567       *    }
2568       *
2569       *    <jc>// Parser that validates inbound values.</jc>
2570       *    ReaderParser <jv>p</jv> = JsonParser.<jsm>create</jsm>().validateSchema().build();
2571       *
2572       *    <jv>p</jv>.read(<js>"{name:'a'}"</js>, MyBean.<jk>class</jk>);  <jc>// throws ParseException - too short</jc>
2573       * </p>
2574       *
2575       * <h5 class='section'>See Also:</h5><ul>
2576       *    <li class='ja'>{@link BeanConfig#validateSchema()}
2577       * </ul>
2578       *
2579       * @return This object.
2580       * @since 10.0.0
2581       */
2582      public Builder validateSchema() {
2583         return validateSchema(true);
2584      }

2588       *

2591       * @since 10.0.0
2592       */

2595         return this;

2625      /**
2626       * Implementation classes.
2627       *
2628       * <p>
2629       * For interfaces and abstract classes this method can be used to specify an implementation class for the
2630       * interface/abstract class so that instances of the implementation class are used when instantiated (e.g. during a
2631       * parse).
2632       *
2633       * <h5 class='section'>Example:</h5>
2634       * <p class='bjava'>
2635       *    <jc>// A bean interface.</jc>
2636       *    <jk>public interface</jk> MyBean {
2637       *       ...
2638       *    }
2639       *
2640       *    <jc>// A bean implementation.</jc>
2641       *    <jk>public class</jk> MyBeanImpl <jk>implements</jk> MyBean {
2642       *       ...
2643       *    }
2644
2645       *    <jc>// Create a parser that instantiates MyBeanImpls when parsing MyBeans.</jc>
2646       *    ReaderParser <jv>parser</jv> = JsonParser
2647       *       .<jsm>create</jsm>()
2648       *       .implClass(MyBean.<jk>class</jk>, MyBeanImpl.<jk>class</jk>)
2649       *       .build();
2650       *
2651       *    <jc>// Instantiates a MyBeanImpl,</jc>
2652       *    MyBean <jv>myBean</jv> = <jv>parser</jv>.read(<js>"..."</js>, MyBean.<jk>class</jk>);
2653       * </p>
2654       *
2655       * @param interfaceClass The interface class.
2656       *    <br>Cannot be <jk>null</jk>.
2657       * @param implClass The implementation class.
2658       *    <br>Cannot be <jk>null</jk>.
2659       * @return This object.
2660       */
2661      public Builder implClass(Class<?> interfaceClass, Class<?> implClass) {
2662         reqnn("interfaceClass", interfaceClass);
2663         reqnn("implClass", implClass);
2664         return annotations(MarshalledApplyAnnotation.create(interfaceClass).value(MarshalledAnnotation.create().implClass(implClass).build()).build());

3143      /**

3146       * <p>

3148       * Calling this method opts out of that behavior so that declaration order is used instead: record component order for records, field declaration order (superclass first) for other classes, then method-only properties alphabetically.

3156       *       <jk>public</jk> String <jf>a</jf> = <js>"3"</js>;
3157       *    }

3159       *    <jc>// Create a serializer that does NOT sort bean properties.</jc>
3160       *    WriterSerializer <jv>serializer</jv> = JsonSerializer
3161       *       .<jsm>create</jsm>()
3162       *       .unsortedProperties()
3163       *       .build();
3164       *
3165       *    <jc>// Produces:  {"c":"1","b":"2","a":"3"} (declaration order)</jc>
3166       *    String <jv>json</jv> = <jv>serializer</jv>.write(<jk>new</jk> MyBean());
3167       * </p>
3168       *
3169       * <h5 class='section'>Notes:</h5><ul>
3170       *    <li class='note'>The {@link BeanType#unsorted() @BeanType.unsorted()} annotation can also be used to opt out of sorting on a single class.
3171       * </ul>
3172       *

3174       */

3176         return unsortedProperties(true);
3177      }

3190      /**

3198       * <h5 class='section'>Example:</h5>
3199       * <p class='bjava'>
3200       *    <jk>public record</jk> Person(String <jv>name</jv>, <jk>int</jk> <jv>age</jv>) {}
3201       *
3202       *    WriterSerializer <jv>serializer</jv> = JsonSerializer
3203       *       .<jsm>create</jsm>()
3204       *       .recordComponentOrder()
3205       *       .build();
3206       *
3207       *    <jc>// Produces:  {"name":"Alice","age":30}</jc>
3208       *    String <jv>json</jv> = <jv>serializer</jv>.write(<jk>new</jk> Person(<js>"Alice"</js>, 30));
3209       * </p>
3210       *
3211       * <h5 class='section'>See Also:</h5><ul>
3212       *    <li class='jm'>{@link #unsortedProperties()} (declaration order for every bean, records included)
3213       *    <li class='ja'>{@link BeanConfig#recordComponentOrder()}
3214       * </ul>
3215       *
3216       * @return This object.
3217       */
3218      public Builder recordComponentOrder() {
3219         return recordComponentOrder(true);
3220      }

3233      /**
3234       * Opt specific bean classes out of alphabetical property sorting.
3235       *
3236       * <p>
3237       * Applies the {@link BeanType#unsorted() @BeanType(unsorted=true)} annotation to the specified classes,
3238       * overriding the default sorted behavior for those specific beans.

3241       *    <li class='ja'>{@link BeanType#unsorted() @BeanType(unsorted)}
3242       * </ul>

3245       *    <br>Cannot contain <jk>null</jk> values.
3246       * @return This object.
3247       */
3248      public Builder unsortedProperties(Class<?>...on) {
3249         reqnns("on", on);

3252         return this;

3255      /**
3256       * Identifies a stop class for the annotated class.
3257       *
3258       * <p>
3259       * Identical in purpose to the stop class specified by {@link Introspector#getBeanInfo(Class, Class)}.
3260       * Any properties in the stop class or in its base classes will be ignored during analysis.
3261       *
3262       * <p>
3263       * For example, in the following class hierarchy, instances of <c>C3</c> will include property <c>p3</c>,
3264       * but not <c>p1</c> or <c>p2</c>.
3265       *
3266       * <h5 class='section'>Example:</h5>
3267       * <p class='bjava'>
3268       *    <jk>public class</jk> C1 {
3269       *       <jk>public int</jk> getP1();
3270       *    }
3271       *
3272       *    <jk>public class</jk> C2 <jk>extends</jk> C1 {
3273       *       <jk>public int</jk> getP2();
3274       *    }
3275       *
3276       *    <jk>public class</jk> C3 <jk>extends</jk> C2 {
3277       *       <jk>public int</jk> getP3();
3278       *    }
3279       *
3280       *    <jc>// Create a serializer specifies a stop class for C3.</jc>
3281       *    WriterSerializer <jv>serializer</jv> = JsonSerializer
3282       *       .<jsm>create</jsm>()
3283       *       .stopClass(C3.<jk>class</jk>, C2.<jk>class</jk>)
3284       *       .build();
3285       *
3286       *    <jc>// Produces:  {"p3":"..."}</jc>
3287       *    String <jv>json</jv> = <jv>serializer</jv>.write(<jk>new</jk> C3());
3288       * </p>
3289       *
3290       * @param on The class on which the stop class is being applied.
3291       *    <br>Cannot be <jk>null</jk>.
3292       * @param value
3293       *    The new value for this setting.
3294       *    <br>Cannot be <jk>null</jk>.
3295       * @return This object.
3296       */
3297      public Builder stopClass(Class<?> on, Class<?> value) {
3298         reqnn("on", on);
3299         reqnn("value", value);
3300         return annotations(BeanTypeApplyAnnotation.create(on).value(BeanTypeAnnotation.create().stopClass(value).build()).build());
3301      }

3303      /**
3304       * A shortcut for defining a {@link FunctionalSwap}.
3305       *
3306       * <h5 class='section'>Example:</h5>
3307       * <p class='bjava'>
3308       *    <jc>// Create a serializer that performs a custom format for DAte objects.</jc>
3309       *    WriterSerializer <jv>serializer</jv> = JsonSerializer
3310       *       .<jsm>create</jsm>()
3311       *       .swap(Date.<jk>class</jk>, String.<jk>class</jk>, <jv>x</jv> -&gt; <jsm>format</jsm>(<jv>x</jv>))
3312       *       .build();
3313       * </p>
3314       *
3315       * @param <T> The object type being swapped out.
3316       * @param <S> The object type being swapped in.
3317       * @param normalClass The object type being swapped out.
3318       *    <br>Cannot be <jk>null</jk>.
3319       * @param swappedClass The object type being swapped in.
3320       *    <br>Cannot be <jk>null</jk>.
3321       * @param swapFunction The function to convert the object.
3322       *    <br>Cannot be <jk>null</jk>.
3323       * @return This object.
3324       */
3325      public <T,S> Builder swap(Class<T> normalClass, Class<S> swappedClass, ThrowingFunction<T,S> swapFunction) {
3326         reqnn("normalClass", normalClass);
3327         reqnn("swappedClass", swappedClass);
3328         reqnn("swapFunction", swapFunction);
3329         swaps().add(0, new FunctionalSwap<>(normalClass, swappedClass, swapFunction, null));
3330         return this;
3331      }

3356       */
3357      public <T,S> Builder swap(Class<T> normalClass, Class<S> swappedClass, ThrowingFunction<T,S> swapFunction, ThrowingFunction<S,T> unswapFunction) {

3398      /**
3399       * Java object swaps.
3400       *
3401       * <p>
3402       * Swaps are used to "swap out" non-serializable classes with serializable equivalents during serialization,
3403       * and "swap in" the non-serializable class during parsing.
3404       *
3405       * <p>
3406       * An example of a swap would be a <c>Calendar</c> object that gets swapped out for an ISO8601 string.
3407       *
3408       * <p>
3409       * Multiple swaps can be associated with a single class.
3410       * When multiple swaps are applicable to the same class, the media type pattern defined by
3411       * {@link ObjectSwap#forMediaTypes()} or {@link Swap#mediaTypes() @Swap(mediaTypes)} are used to come up with the best match.
3412       *
3413       * <p>
3414       * Values can consist of any of the following types:
3415       * <ul>
3416       *    <li>Any subclass of {@link ObjectSwap}.
3417       *    <li>Any instance of {@link ObjectSwap}.
3418       *    <li>Any surrogate class.  A shortcut for defining a {@link SurrogateSwap}.
3419       *    <li>Any array or collection of the objects above.
3420       * </ul>
3421       *
3422       * <h5 class='section'>Example:</h5>
3423       * <p class='bjava'>
3424       *    <jc>// Sample swap for converting Dates to ISO8601 strings.</jc>
3425       *    <jk>public class</jk> MyDateSwap <jk>extends</jk> StringSwap&lt;Date&gt; {
3426       *       <jc>// ISO8601 formatter.</jc>
3427       *       <jk>private</jk> DateFormat <jf>format</jf> = <jk>new</jk> SimpleDateFormat(<js>"yyyy-MM-dd'T'HH:mm:ssZ"</js>);
3428       *
3429       *       <ja>@Override</ja>
3430       *       <jk>public</jk> String swap(MarshallingSession <jv>session</jv>, Date <jv>date</jv>) {
3431       *          <jk>return</jk> <jf>format</jf>.format(<jv>date</jv>);
3432       *       }
3433       *
3434       *       <ja>@Override</ja>
3435       *       <jk>public</jk> Date unswap(MarshallingSession <jv>session</jv>, String <jv>string</jv>, ClassMeta <jv>hint</jv>) <jk>throws</jk> Exception {
3436       *          <jk>return</jk> <jf>format</jf>.parse(<jv>string</jv>);
3437       *       }
3438       *    }
3439       *
3440       *    <jc>// Sample bean with a Date field.</jc>
3441       *    <jk>public class</jk> MyBean {
3442       *       <jk>public</jk> Date <jf>date</jf> = <jk>new</jk> Date(112, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6);
3443       *    }
3444       *
3445       *    <jc>// Create a serializer that uses our date swap.</jc>
3446       *    WriterSerializer <jv>serializer</jv> = JsonSerializer
3447       *       .<jsm>create</jsm>()
3448       *       .swaps(MyDateSwap.<jk>class</jk>)
3449       *       .build();
3450       *
3451       *    <jc>// Produces:  {"date":"2012-03-03T04:05:06-0500"}</jc>
3452       *    String <jv>json</jv> = <jv>serializer</jv>.write(<jk>new</jk> MyBean());
3453       *
3454       *    <jc>// Create a serializer that uses our date swap.</jc>
3455       *    ReaderParser <jv>parser</jv> = JsonParser
3456       *       .<jsm>create</jsm>()
3457       *       .swaps(MyDateSwap.<jk>class</jk>)
3458       *       .build();
3459       *
3460       *    <jc>// Use our parser to parse a bean.</jc>
3461       *    MyBean <jv>bean</jv> = <jv>parser</jv>.read(<jv>json</jv>, MyBean.<jk>class</jk>);
3462       * </p>
3463       *
3464       * <h5 class='section'>Notes:</h5><ul>
3465       *    <li class='note'>The {@link Swap @Swap} annotation can also be used on classes to identify swaps for the class.
3466       *    <li class='note'>The {@link Swap @Swap} annotation can also be used on bean methods and fields to identify swaps for values of those bean properties.
3467       * </ul>
3468       *
3469       * @param values
3470       *    The values to add to this setting.
3471       *    <br>Values can consist of any of the following types:
3472       *    <ul>
3473       *       <li>Any subclass of {@link ObjectSwap}.
3474       *       <li>Any surrogate class.  A shortcut for defining a {@link SurrogateSwap}.
3475       *       <li>Any array/collection/stream of the objects above.
3476       *    </ul>
3477       *    <br>Cannot be <jk>null</jk>.
3478       * @return This object.
3479       */
3480      public Builder swaps(Object...values) {
3481         reqnns("values", values);
3482         swaps().addAll(0, accumulate(values));
3483         return this;
3484      }

3486      /**
3487       * <i><l>Context</l> configuration property:&emsp;</i>  TimeZone.
3488       *
3489       * <p>
3490       * Specifies the default time zone for serializer and parser sessions when not specified via {@link MarshallingSession.Builder#timeZone(TimeZone)}.
3491       * Typically used for POJO swaps that need to deal with timezones such as swaps that convert <l>Date</l> and <l>Calendar</l>
3492       * objects to strings by accessing it via the session passed into the {@link ObjectSwap#swap(MarshallingSession, Object)} and
3493       * {@link ObjectSwap#unswap(MarshallingSession, Object, ClassMeta, String)} methods.
3494       *
3495       * <h5 class='section'>Example:</h5>
3496       * <p class='bjava'>
3497       *    <jc>// Define a POJO swap that skips serializing beans if the time zone is GMT.</jc>
3498       *    <jk>public class</jk> MyBeanSwap <jk>extends</jk> StringSwap&lt;MyBean&gt; {
3499       *       <ja>@Override</ja>
3500       *       <jk>public</jk> String swap(MarshallingSession <jv>session</jv>, MyBean <jv>bean</jv>) <jk>throws</jk> Exception {
3501       *          <jk>if</jk> (<jv>session</jv>.getTimeZone().equals(TimeZone.<jsf>GMT</jsf>))
3502       *             <jk>return null</jk>;
3503       *          <jk>return</jk> <jv>bean</jv>.toString();
3504       *       }
3505       *    }
3506       *
3507       *    <jc>// Create a serializer that uses GMT if the timezone is not specified in the session args.</jc>
3508       *    WriterSerializer <jv>serializer</jv> = JsonSerializer
3509       *       .<jsm>create</jsm>()
3510       *       .timeZone(TimeZone.<jsf>GMT</jsf>)
3511       *       .build();
3512       * </p>
3513       *
3514       * <h5 class='section'>See Also:</h5><ul>
3515       *    <li class='ja'>{@link MarshalledConfig#timeZone()}
3516       *    <li class='jm'>{@link MarshallingSession.Builder#timeZone(TimeZone)}
3517       * </ul>
3518       *
3519       * @param value The new value for this property.
3520       *    <br>Can be <jk>null</jk> (timezone will not be set, defaults to system timezone).
3521       * @return This object.
3522       */
3523      public Builder timeZone(TimeZone value) {
3524         timeZone = value;
3525         return this;
3526      }

3786      /**
3787       * An identifying name for this class.
3788       *
3789       * <p>

3791       * For example, if a bean property is of type <c>Object</c>, then the serializer will add the name to the
3792       * output so that the class can be determined during parsing.

3798       * <p class='bjava'>
3799       *    <jc>// Use _type='mybean' to identify this bean.</jc>

3802       *    <jc>// Create a serializer and specify the type name..</jc>
3803       *    WriterSerializer <jv>serializer</jv> = JsonSerializer
3804       *       .<jsm>create</jsm>()
3805       *       .typeName(MyBean.<jk>class</jk>, <js>"mybean"</js>)
3806       *       .build();

3808       *    <jc>// Produces:  {"_type":"mybean",...}</jc>

3826       *    <br>Cannot be <jk>null</jk>.
3827       * @return This object.

3829      public Builder typeName(Class<?> on, String value) {

4027   /**
4028    * Checks if the specified class should be cached.
4029    *
4030    * <p>
4031    * Generated classes (proxies, lambda expressions, etc.) shouldn't be cacheable to prevent
4032    * needlessly filling up the cache.
4033    *
4034    * @param c The class to check.
4035    * @return <jk>true</jk> if the class should be cached.
4036    */
4037   private static boolean isCacheable(Class<?> c) {
4038      var n = c.getName();
4039      var x = n.charAt(n.length() - 1);  // All generated classes appear to end with digits.
4040      return !((x >= '0' && x <= '9') && (n.indexOf("$$") != -1 || n.startsWith("sun") || n.startsWith("com.sun") || n.indexOf("$Proxy") != -1));
4041   }

4345   /**
4346    * Fallback for an ObjectSwap-conversion whose swap-class doesn't bridge to the input, but where the input
4347    * is already a {@link Map} matching the target's own Map shape -- copies its entries into a new instance
4348    * of the target type rather than dropping the value as {@code null}.
4349    *
4350    * @param toMeta The target type.
4351    * @param in The input value.
4352    * @return A new map instance of the target type populated with the input's entries, or <jk>null</jk> if
4353    *    the target isn't Map-shaped or the input isn't a {@link Map}.
4354    */
4355   private static Object copyMapEntries(ClassMeta<?> toMeta, Object in) {
4356      if (! (toMeta.isMap() && in instanceof Map<?,?> in2))
4357         return null;
4358      var result = (Map<Object,Object>) (toMeta.canCreateNewInstance() ? toMeta.newInstance() : new LinkedHashMap<>());
4359      result.putAll(in2);
4360      return result;
4361   }
